- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)

- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

# Pull Request Information

- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

{
  "key": "pr-1137",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)",
    "description": "Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)"

Depends on TranscriptMarkdown.formatLine — an empty line likely yields one empty row. Likely fine.

But there's a subtler issue: `stickyIndex` is clamped in `_echoEndRow` against `starts.length - 1`. If outputLines gets FRONT-TRIMMED during a long run (scrollback cap), stickyIndex could exceed starts.length → clamp handles it. OK.

The `clamp(0, starts.length - 1)` empty-list edge: starts empty requires outputLines empty → only before any submit... but sticky armed requires stickyIndex >= 0 with stickyLines non-empty, set only on submit of non-empty text, which appends the echo to outputLines. bool get _stickyActive {

  final starts = _wrapCache.lineStartRows;
  final echoEndLine = (stickyIndex + stickyEchoLineCount).clamp(0, starts.length - 1);

Only via front-trim if cap small; the echo is at the tail — trim keeps the tail. So starts non-empty. Fine — same as pre-fix. Not a finding beyond maybe a defensive SUGGESTION.

3. **Performance**: `_framePlanFor` is called 2-3× per frame (view, _scrollBottom via _viewportHeight, _writeScrollIndicator via _scrollBottom). The dedupe adds `_wrappedLines()` (cache hit) + `_echoEndRow()` (cache hit + clamp) per call — O(1). Fine. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1137
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1137
- **Title**: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-917` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +122
- **Deletions**: -18
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T22:03:22Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T23:23:22Z

## PR Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. # pr-1137: fix(#917): deterministic wrap-turn dedupe in TUI composer (no double-paint on slow PTY)

## Description

Fixes #917

## Race

The composer's wrap-turn dedupe — whether the sticky turn echo pins or the transcript window owns it — keyed on the RAW stored `scrollOffset` (`_stickyActive`), while `view()` paints at the freshly computed follow bottom (`_scrollBottom(wrapped)`). Keystrokes re-wrap the composer input between output events: the input zone grows/shrinks, the frame plan's history height moves, the painted window top moves — the stored offset does not (keystroke handlers never touch it). Under slow/racy PTY timing a backspace burst lands after the last streamed flush, dropping the painted window top back onto the echo text while the stale raw offset still reported the echo fully scrolled out: the same turn row painted twice (pinned AND in the transcript). The mirrored interleave lost the echo entirely (unpinned, above the window).

## Fix

`_framePlanFor` now decides the pin from the geometry the frame will actually paint — the follow bottom, or the stored offset when detached — computed with the pin's own rows taken, against the echo's wrapped end row (`_echoEndRow`). Both candidate heights are already in scope inside the plan, so the old recursion concern ("the plan needs sticky, sticky would need the plan's viewport") does not apply. Result: the echo paints exactly once — pinned iff the painted window cannot show it — under any event interleaving; the raw offset is no longer consulted for the dedupe.

## Repro / verification

Headless, real controller pipeline (FaTuiModel.update driving KeyMsg/OutputMsg/BusyMsg — no openpty): submit → stream past the echo → type an 8-row wrapped draft mid-run → one streamed line (offset syncs past the echo, draft present) → backspace burst. Pre-fix the final frame contains the echo twice; post-fix exactly once. Regression test added in `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` (both chrome modes); fails on main, passes with the fix.

- `test/cli/fa_tui_sticky_scroll_test.dart` 4/4 (2 pre-existing + 2 new)
- Targeted TUI family `test/cli/fa_tui_*.dart` + `tui_*.dart`: all green except 7 pre-existing failures (prototype snapshot + live-PTY suites, host-unrunnable — verified identical on unpatched main via stash)
- Scoped `dart analyze` on the three touched files: clean (one pre-existing unnecessary_import info, present on main)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…
